item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Something along the lines of the following then?

Computers with SCP-096-J enabled will be unable to display sexually explicit material due to the program's ability to remove explicit components from audiovisual and literary works. This function will operate when possible by editing the narrative of the materials into scenarios wherein sexual congress or situations are unlikely or altering the decisions of actors within the narrative to remove sexual activity.

The similarity between the effects of SCP-096-J and those of SCP-1781 have been noted and it is possible that both anomalies operate by a similar mechanism, or were created by the same entity or entities.

item.title: Re: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Normally I'm not really interested in adding links to serious articles into joke articles, but in this case it's a funny-enough mainlister and a straightfaced-enough joke article that I can see it.

Given that 096-J's tone is basically the same as that of a mainlister, I think an explicit mention of SCP-1781 inserted a sentence before "See Experiment Log 096-J for examples." would be perfectly fine and less weird.

item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Edits made per discussion below. Timer removed. Edits may be reverted by the author at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 72 hours if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

So, reading the effect of this anomaly, even though its in a -J article, reminds me of SCP-1781 in how it manages to alter narrative/content of work. Since I don't want to mess with the flow of any of the jokes in the article, I'm recommending a simple inline link:

Editing the following:

This function will operate when possible by editing the narrative of the materials into scenarios wherein sexual congress or situations are unlikely or altering the decisions of actors within the narrative to remove sexual activity.

To this:

This function will operate when possible by editing the narrative of the materials into scenarios wherein sexual congress or situations are unlikely or altering the decisions of actors within the narrative to remove sexual activity.

In this sense the link highlights the ability of both anomalies to edit preexisting narratives in one manner or another.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

Experiment ID: 096-F-20/H

Sample: A 1000-word Harry Potter fan-written fiction titled "The Potion Mishap", uploaded to ███████████████.org on ██/██/12

Parameters: SCP-096-J set to "Full Limit"

Results: Harry Potter sits in his Potions class learning how to make a potion. As Professor Snape comes over to examine his cauldron, Draco Malfoy throws an unknown ingredient into Harry's cauldron. The cauldron explodes, and both Harry and Professor Snape are covered in the potion.

Professor Snape takes this opportunity to teach the class the correct procedures for safe potion removal and disposal, as set by the Wizarding Health and Safety Commission. After carefully removing the potion from both himself and Harry, he disposes of the potion safely, and then quizzes the class on the best way to safely remove a variety of potions.

Harry and the other students leave the class feeling enlightened on correct potion safety protocol.
